Survival Phase (End of Round) 1.4 Combat & Dice 1.5 Equipment & Symbols 1.6 End of Game Rumble Planet Rumble Planet is a battle-royale board game where players act as contestants in an intergalactic TV show. The goal is to gain the most Fame (Prestige) while the planet crumbles beneath the fighters' feet. Game Objective The winner is the player with the most Fame Points (Prestige) at the end of the game. Points are earned by attacking opponents, collecting gear, and surviving in shrinking zones. Game Setup The board consists of modular areas (zones). Each player chooses a character with unique stats for Hit Points (HP), Movement, and special abilities. Equipment cards (Weapons, Armor, Gadgets) are prepared. Game Flow The game is played over several rounds. Each round consists of two main phases: 1. Action Phase (Player Turns) Players take turns in sequence. During a turn, a player has 3 Actions that can be chosen flexibly from the following options (can be repeated): Move: Move the character up to the maximum movement range of their profile. Search (Loot): Draw an equipment card from the deck or the current space. Attack: Attack an opponent within range (Melee or Ranged). Equip/Use: Put on gear or activate gadgets. Interact: Interact with special terrain tiles or mission objectives. 2. Survival Phase (End of Round) After all players have finished their turns: The Zone Shrinks: Certain areas of the board are marked as "Danger Zones" or removed. Players in these zones take massive damage. Replenish: New equipment appears on the map. Check Initiative: The turn order for the next round is determined. Combat & Dice Combat is usually resolved through dice rolls: Attack Value: The number of dice is determined by the character stat + bonuses from weapons. Defense: The defender uses their base value + armor bonuses. Damage: Each unblocked success reduces the opponent's Hit Points (HP) and grants Fame to the attacker. Equipment & Symbols Items are divided into three categories: Weapons (Red): Increase damage or range. Armor (Blue): Protect against incoming damage. Gadgets (Yellow): One-time effects or tactical advantages (e.g., teleportation). Important symbols on cards: Crosshair: Range of the attack. Lightning Bolt: Immediate effect or bonus action. Shield: Defense bonus. Star: Fame point bonus. End of Game The game ends when only one player is left (all others eliminated) or a set number of rounds has been reached. In case of elimination, the survivor does not necessarily win; the victory goes to the player with the highest Prestige score . [Rating: 2/10] Another lame attempt at a battle royale board game. Unimpressive and anticlimactic.

[Rating: 5/10] Initial impression from TTS play during campaign. Similar to Adrenaline, map movement and pinging folks for points. No significant penalty for dying and no player elimination. Looked through the weapon, armor, and loot decks. Didnt see many bonkers powers and the loot card variance is really low. This is likely to be a somewhat dry points race.

[Rating: 8/10] Game with a wacky universe, very interesting mechanics concerning the use of portals and the reappearance of loot boxes on the board. The board is very cool with these pieces that give relief to the terrain. The playable characters during the presentation of the Spiel Essen 2024 show already have a story of their own and it makes you want to discover the rest of the game!
